CanBeGeneratedInCombat.issue: Closed 2026-07-31 (tier-2 campaign): Flag pair corrected against the C#, read line-by-line for all six cards: none overrides CanBeGeneratedByModifiers or CanonicalKeywords, so the sim's is_playable=False AND can_be_generated_by_modifiers=False were BOTH wrong and can_be_generated_in_combat=False was missing. These Statuses are playable no-effect cards in the game (the shape the sim already models for card/beckon). LIVENESS CORRECTION: the recorded dormancy checked only pool_card_ids and curse_pool_ids, but a THIRD consumer exists -- transform_options_in_combat's STATUS branch, reached by ported Entropy. Pre-fix this genuinely leaked all four bad cards as transform options for every reachable Status card, including frantic_escape, which The Insatiable really does put in piles (test_hive.py::TestTheInsatiable). Reproduced by execution by both the implementer and the task reviewer, and closed by the same fix -- the STATUS branch's filter is the correct mirror of GetFilteredTransformationOptions (CardFactory.cs:189-203). So this mechanism was recorded DORMANT but was reachable; it is fixed, not merely re-argued. Pinned in test/test_card_generation_pool.py.  The text it replaced read: `public override bool CanBeGeneratedInCombat => false` (NeowsFury.cs:15) has no `can_be_generated_in_combat = False` counterpart; the sim's comment says the ANCIENT rarity already keeps it out of `pool_card_ids`. That is true today, so the OUTCOME matches -- but it is a different mechanism, and the flag is the one C# actually exposes: `CardModel.CanBeGeneratedInCombat` (CardModel.cs:642) is read by FilterForCombat regardless of rarity, so any future in-combat generator pointed at a pool that includes Ancients would pick up Neow's Fury in the sim and not in the game. DORMANT with the trigger named. Contrast card/feed, card/hand_of_greed and card/hidden_gem, which set the flag explicitly, and card/disintegration / card/frantic_escape / card/mind_rot, which set the WRONG flag -- three different treatments of one override across six cards.

OnPlay.issue: Closed (re-audited 2026-08-04, stale-sweep task-8 batch-04): the file was substantially rewritten since the 2026-07-26 audit. TWO things changed and both close the previously-recorded gap. (1) The card no longer needs its own self-exclusion predicate: round 13 (R5) made the sim's Play pile real, so a resolving card is no longer parked in the discard pile (neows_fury.py:23-29) -- same de-hack as headbutt.py. (2) `CombatState.select_cards` (combat.py:1475 on) now models `min_select` / `CardSelectorPrefs.MinSelect` as a genuine parameter: `require_manual_confirmation = min_select is not None and min_select != count` and the auto-select shortcut floor becomes `min_select` instead of `count` (combat.py:1551-1559), matching `RequireManualConfirmation`'s derivation (CardSelectorPrefs.cs:77) and the C# shortcut condition `!RequireManualConfirmation && candidateCount <= MinSelect` (CardSelectCmd.cs:287-290/396-399/708-711). The card's own `on_play` now calls `CardSelectCmd.from_pile(..., count=count, min_select=0)` (neows_fury.py:72-75), which is the exact `new CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 0, num)` MinSelect-0/MaxSelect-num range C# builds (NeowsFury.cs:39) -- so the player may now decline part or all of the return on both sides, and the previously-missing MIN half of the range is modeled. `MAX_HAND_SIZE` is still 10 on both sides (CardPile.cs:21, player.py:68 -- was cited :56, decompiler/line-shift drift only). Attack-then-select order unchanged and still faithful.
